question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a coefficient of zero, as follows:

$$
{x}^{4}-3{x}^{2}+2x+1={x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2x+1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}+2x\,\,\,\,\, \\  & {x}^{2}-2x+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+0{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+2x+1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+2x+1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+2x+0}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

  

As a result, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}+2x,$ and

- the remainder is $1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{4}-3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{{x}^{2}-2x+1} & ={x}^{2}+2x+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}-2x+1} \\ .\end{aligned}
$$
